actions.label: Provide food rations to guards and their families as compensation
Commit to no skimming of food for guards and equal rations for all refugees, including those labelled terrorists
Permit FWB's nutritional assessment under camp-provided escort and security
Allow FWB staff unescorted, unrestricted movement inside the camp
Allow refugee consultation on needs and prioritise hiring host-town local actors
Give existing guard/militia structures a role in organizing and implementing distribution
Maintain camp perimeter, containment and generator fuel arrangements during the aid operation
Allow FWB to communicate and document its work publicly within agreed security limits
Conduct, drop or scale down the donor-required nutritional assessments
Deliver ongoing, recurring food aid shipments to the camp
Accept that all FWB presence in the camp is coordinated and escorted
Distribute food block by block on a schedule agreed with camp security

goals.label: Food aid serves as camp currency or payment
Commander's personal safety and legal exposure
Host town's economy and goodwill are protected
Refugees receive the intended food without diversion
Burdensome outside assessments and procedures in the camp
Camp authorities and militia control food distribution
Camp generators and fuel keep running
Commander's authority and standing before guards
FWB neutrality preserved, aid not feeding or paying armed actors
FWB staff and local assistants are safe from harm
FWB staff have sufficient access and movement in the camp
Food is distributed fairly without excluding groups labelled terrorists
Guard discipline and loyalty hold, without rebellion or violence
Guards and their families are fed and compensated despite unpaid salaries
Hostile actors exploit outside access or aid
Ongoing food aid reaches the camp
Outsiders move freely and unescorted inside the camp
Refugees stay contained and do not reach the capital
Refugees' nutritional needs are assessed and documented
Donor requirements met so funding continues
FWB's reputation and public visibility
Refugees have a say in the aid response

redLines.label: Allow FWB and its chosen local assistants to manage food distribution directly instead of guards
redLines.quote: If FWB brings in local independent workers to hand out the food, you can't trust those people not to stir up trouble and maybe even help hidden terrorists by passing along supplies or information.

redLines.label: Have FWB staff and FWB-chosen local assistants manage food disbursement directly
redLines.quote: If FWB brings in local independent workers to hand out the food, you can't trust those people not to stir up trouble and maybe even help hidden terrorists by passing along supplies or information.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
